verdict.rationale: LaunchDarkly lists a first-party "Code references" capability. Hands-on users corroborate that it answers where a flag is used in code, and that LD analytics surface stale or unused flags, flags only evaluated to the default, and temporary versus permanent flags. First-party documentation in the pack is only a section title, so the depth of the workflow is mostly evidenced by community reports. Missing for 10: in-depth first-party docs on stale-flag detection and code-reference scanning setup, and evidence of a documented cleanup/removal workflow.

support.subject: As a platform engineer, I can find stale flags and code references so temporary flags actually get removed from the codebase

citations.quote: LaunchDarkly even has a product feature that does this, called 'Code References.'
flagging unused flags, flags only ever evaluated to the default, or to one outcome
its analytics for spotting stale flags and marking temporary vs permanent ones to reduce tech debt
